track_b_contribution: Track B contains no comparable action-effect evidence capable of reweighting structural breadth.
integrated_conclusion: Indofood remains the breadth leader on the validated Track A definition.
critical_caveat: Breadth is not category breadth or strategy effectiveness.

track_a_conclusion: Unilever leads 3 of 5 complete selected focal-category snapshots and Wings leads 2 of 5.
track_b_contribution: No defensible action-level explanation is established for those group-level leadership observations.
integrated_conclusion: Selected-category leadership remains a Track A outcome rather than a validated result of specific actions.
critical_caveat: Selected focal-category leadership is not market share.

track_a_conclusion: Wings leads observed stability in 4 of 5 comparable blocks; momentum leadership is split between Indofood and Unilever at 2 blocks each and Wings at 1.
track_b_contribution: Track B evidence is too sparse and granularly mismatched to explain the block-level pattern.
integrated_conclusion: Track A stability and momentum leaders remain unchanged.
critical_caveat: Stability is not strength and momentum magnitudes are not averaged across categories.

track_a_conclusion: Unilever retains all three observed incumbent opportunities; Indofood loses its one observed opportunity; Wings records one challenger takeover.
track_b_contribution: No screened action-result chain defensibly explains these role-specific outcomes.
integrated_conclusion: Persistence remains an observed Track A competitive-role outcome.

track_a_conclusion: Track A does not score strategy effectiveness.
track_b_contribution: Track B yields one direct descriptive pair, four temporal action pairs, two company-reported action screenings, one reporting-perimeter context case, and fourteen not-assessable actions.
integrated_conclusion: Strategy-result evidence is case-specific and disclosure-sensitive rather than a cross-group effect scale.
critical_caveat: Evidence-class counts measure assessability, not success.

track_a_conclusion: A single overall portfolio winner is not defensible because validated dimensions have different leaders and no common defensible scale/weighting exists.
track_b_contribution: Track B adds heterogeneous case-level evidence but no comparable cross-group strategy-effect scale.
integrated_conclusion: Combined evidence continues to support dimension-specific leaders rather than one overall winner.
critical_caveat: A richer narrative does not justify post-hoc weighting.
